prompt: Some employers offer their employees subsidized membership of gym or sports clubs, believing that this will make their staff healthier and thus more effective at work. Other employers see no benefit in so doing. Discuss both views and give your opinion. Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own experience or knowledge.
essay: Some employers help cover the cost of fitness club memberships for their workers. However, other companies believe this is not a worthwhile investment. I believe it can save a lot of money on healthcare, it can boost morale and improve mental wellbeing. On one hand, employers who support gym memberships argue that this leads to healthier employees, which can reduce sick days and improve productivity. For example, employees who exercise and consume healthy food can prevent various diseases such as obesity, which can lead to high blood pressure, diabetes, higher cancer risk and liver disease. Healthier employees can lead to a positive company culture. For example, employees often share positive experiences about their workplace with others, which strengthens the company's reputation. Working in an environment where people care about their health and mental state can inspire others to do the same, creating a more motivated team. On the other hand, some employers believe that spending money on gym memberships is a waste if employees do not take advantage of the benefit. They argue that not everyone enjoys going to the gym or that some may prefer other forms of exercise, like walking or cycling. Another point of view is that the money used for gym memberships could be better spent on training or improving work conditions. Employers might believe that these changes will have a more direct impact on productivity and job satisfaction. Additionally, this approach does not always succeed, as some employees choose not to use these benefits. In conclusion, while some employers believe that subsidized gym memberships are better spent elsewhere, others argue that they can improve employee health. In my opinion, subsidized gym memberships are a worthwhile investment for employers, as they can reduce healthcare costs and improve staff morale and mental wellbeing.
